newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Sentiment bullish but cautious.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Sentiment bullish but cautious.

text.p: As the U.S. stock market extends recent gains, options investors and traders remain bullish, but high premium levels suggest investors are cautious, traders said Tuesday.
The high premiums are also keeping volume on the low side as investors are less inclined to take big risks.
"Premiums are just too high to take any kind of shot," one S&P 100 index .OEX options trader said.
He said the steep premiums, as well as indicating the amount of risk in the market, are a disincentive because of the hefty price a wrong-way bet carries.
For example, the OEX March 790 calls, the most active OEX call option with volume of 3,200 by about 1100 CST/1700 GMT, was trading at nine, up 1/8 on the day.
The spot OEX was up nearly a point at 788.43, making those calls at-the-money.
The March 790 put was trading at 2-5/16, up 3/16.
The most active OEX put was the March 770, with volume of more than 7,700 contracts. It was unchanged at 3-1/2.
"There's a lot of premium in this market," one S&P 500 index .SPX options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said.
The trader added that some investors, expecting a decline, were buying puts below the market.
The SPX was off about a point at 812.75 after climbing to nearly 815.
"Right now, downside puts are getting offered," the trader said, citing speculation that weak bond prices would take the stock market lower.
The OEX options trader said if bonds continue to erode, stocks would likely follow suit.
"But I still believe we're in a bull run," the SPX trader said. "I think the market's going up."
The SPX trader said pre-expiration week has generally been a good one for stocks. March index options expire at the end of next week.
He said that while some investors were buying puts for protection, others, mostly institutional investors, were buying calls at the 800 and 810 strikes in March.
At the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the March 810 calls were among the most active SPX calls, with turnover of 3,185 contracts.
The heaviest volume was in the September 750 and 810 calls, which traded 16,050 and 15,981 contracts, respectively.
One SPX trader at the CBOE said an institution was selling the September 750/810 call spread.
"It's a repeat from the last couple of days," he said. "He's been an active seller."
Heavy turnover was also seen in the SPX June 735 calls and puts, each of which traded about 5,000 contracts. Most of the volume crossed as spreads.
Open interest in those contracts rose by about 19,700 contracts each on Monday.
"The good times keep going," one strategist said.
((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
